refund: Refunds are issued only after the billing team confirms an error on the account. The draft may say the account will be reviewed and that the customer will be contacted with the outcome within 7 business days. Do not promise a refund, a refund amount, or a refund date. Approved refunds are applied as a credit on the next bill unless the customer requests a check.
outage: Customers whose service was interrupted for more than 24 consecutive hours may be eligible for a prorated outage credit, applied automatically to the next bill after the outage is verified. The draft may say the customer may be eligible and that eligibility is confirmed after verification. Do not state a credit amount. If the outage is ongoing, direct the customer to the 24-hour service line for status updates and to report any safety hazard immediately.
shutoff: If a customer reports their service was shut off, the draft must not state why it was shut off or confirm that it was in error. It may say the account is being reviewed with priority. Residential shutoffs lasting more than 48 hours, or any shutoff involving a medical need, small children, or elderly residents, must be escalated (see escalation policy). Restoration timelines may only be given if a staff comment provides them.
billing: Customers may dispute any charge on their bill. While a dispute is open, late fees are not applied to the disputed amount, but the undisputed portion remains due on the original due date. Residential customers may request a payment plan of up to 6 months. The draft may explain these options but must not say a charge is incorrect before the billing team reviews it.
damage: Property damage claims require a completed claim form and supporting photos or receipts. Claims are investigated and the customer is contacted within 10 business days of receiving the form. The draft must not admit fault or liability, must not promise compensation, and should tell the customer how to submit a claim form if they have not already done so.
escalation: Escalate to a supervisor when a complaint involves a health or safety risk, a residential shutoff over 48 hours, a medical need, a threat of legal action, media or regulator involvement, or a third complaint on the same issue within 30 days. For escalated complaints, the draft should acknowledge the seriousness of the issue and state that a supervisor will contact the customer within 1 business day. Do not mention legal action or regulators in the draft, even if the customer did.
